title: Authorization Delegation and Evidence Cadence Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose
This playbook describes standardized patterns for delegated authorization, scheduled evidence collection (the ‘evidence cadence’), and how RBAC, audit logging, data residency, secure SDLC, and incident response interact when an exception or delegation is approved. It is intended for security engineers, compliance owners, SREs, and product teams operating Redwood-managed and customer-hosted deployments.

Scope
- Applies to service identities, human privileged roles, API keys, and temporary delegations (just-in-time/admin-activation).
- Covers evidence collection cadence for audits and incident requests across regions (US/EU/APAC).
- Integrates observability queries and packaging instructions for compliance evidence repositories.

Quick summary of responsibilities
- Authorization Owner (security): maintain policy templates, run quarterly certification.
- Service Owner (platform/product): implement least-privilege principals and review exception requests.
- SRE/Oncall: produce runtime audit bundles on request within 48 hours.
- Compliance SME: validate evidence packages for regulators.

Key definitions
- Delegation: a scoped, time-bound authorization granted to a principal (human/service) to perform actions outside their default role.
- Evidence Cadence: the scheduled and ad-hoc process by which audit artifacts (logs, config snapshots, approvals) are assembled and retained to satisfy compliance requests and post-incident forensics.
- Exception: an approved deviation from standard policy (timeboxed with remediation tasks).

High-level policy statements
1) Delegations must be time-bound with explicit expiry (max 30 days for privileged human delegation; max 7 days for service-level elevated tokens unless automated rotation is enforced).
2) All delegation actions must be logged with a consistent audit schema (see Audit Log Schema below).
3) Requests for evidence must be acknowledged within 24 hours and full packaged evidence delivered within 48 hours for internal audits, and 72 hours for regulated external audits unless otherwise negotiated.
4) Evidence retention for delegation-related artifacts: default 7 years for regulated customers, 2 years for Redwood internal_development artifacts; retention is governed by the Data Residency Matrix in this playbook.

Delegation patterns and recommended RBAC constructs
- Pattern A: Role-based scoped delegation (preferred)
  - Create a narrow role (e.g., support-dump-read-us-east) with minimal actions.
  - Delegate via Access Request system (JIT) that requires manager approval + 2FA.
- Pattern B: Temporary token issuance (machine-to-machine)
  - Use short-lived tokens (TTL 1 hour) issued by internal token broker with mandatory rotation via the service identity manager.
- Pattern C: Emergency break-glass
  - Requires documented justification, two approvers (oncall lead + security oncall), and automatic audit flagging. Post-use, a 7-day forensic review is mandatory.

RBAC policy template (example)
| Role | Actions | Resources | Max delegation TTL | Approval channel |
|------|---------|-----------|--------------------|------------------|
| support-dump-read | read:logs, read:metrics | infra:clusters/*/namespaces/support | 8 hours | access.redwood.com/jit |
| svc-elevate-temp | write:deploy | infra:clusters/{cluster}/services/{svc} | 1 hour | token-broker |

Audit log schema (required fields)
- timestamp (RFC3339)
- request_id (uuid)
- principal_id (user:email or service:{id})
- principal_type (human|service|system)
- action (string; canonical verb)
- resource (string)
- delegation_id (nullable; links to delegation request)
- approval_chain (array of approver ids)
- decision (granted|denied|revoked)
- justification (text)
- correlation_id (incident_id or change_id)
- geo_region (us|eu|apac)

Sample audit log event (JSON example)
{
  "timestamp": "2029-02-11T14:32:08Z",
  "request_id": "6e8b2f9a-3a2f-4d1b-9f9e-1bb9c7f8b4a0",
  "principal_id": "alice@redwood.ai",
  "principal_type": "human",
  "action": "assume:role",
  "resource": "role:support-dump-read-us-east",
  "delegation_id": "deleg-20290211-42",
  "approval_chain": ["manager:jonah.kim", "security:asha.patel"],
  "decision": "granted",
  "justification": "Customer incident TKT-1248 - need logs for triage",
  "correlation_id": "incident-TKT-1248",
  "geo_region": "us"
}

Evidence cadence (scheduled and on-demand processes)
1) Quarterly certification (recurring):
   - Frequency: every 90 days.
   - Owner: Authorization Owner (security).
   - Outputs: role inventory CSV, last-90d delegation summary, outstanding exceptions list, certification tickets for remediations.
2) Monthly logging sanity check:
   - Owner: SRE Observability.
   - Outputs: retention adherence report, missing-field alerts (if audit schema fields missing), sample queries.
3) On-demand evidence request (audit or incident):
   - Acknowledge within 24 hours.
   - Assemble: audit logs (timebox +/-72 hours around event), delegation artifacts (request/approval records), relevant config snapshots (RBAC policy at time T), and chain-of-custody manifest.
   - Deliver packaged evidence to secure bucket with HSM-wrapped encryption and append to compliance evidence index.

Evidence packaging manifest (required files for every package)
- manifest.json (metadata: who assembled, timestamps, package_id)
- audit_events.ndjson (sorted by timestamp)
- delegation_requests.csv (including delegation_id, TTL, approvers, justification)
- rbac_snapshot.yaml (RBAC policy versions and hash)
- chain_of_custody.txt (human-readable steps and checksums)
- retention_policy.txt (which retention applies and why)

Sample manifest.json (fields, as text)
{
  "package_id": "evidence-2029-02-11-0001",
  "assembled_by": "sre-oncall@redwood.ai",
  "assembly_time": "2029-02-11T18:12:00Z",
  "scope": "incident-TKT-1248",
  "regions": ["us"],
  "files": ["audit_events.ndjson", "delegation_requests.csv", "rbac_snapshot.yaml"]
}

Audit query recipes
- Splunk/Kusto: find delegations for a user in past 30 days
  - KQL: AuditLogs | where principal_id==\"alice@redwood.ai\" and action contains \"assume:role\" | where timestamp > ago(30d) | project timestamp, request_id, delegation_id, decision, justification
- Elastic: find emergency delegations in EU region
  - Query: {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"geo_region":"eu"}},{"match":{"action":"break-glass"}}]}}}

Data residency and retention mapping (summary table)
- Redwood internal development artifacts: 2 years (default)
- Customer regulated artifacts (per-customer contract): as specified (commonly 7 years)
- Emergency break-glass evidence: retain 7 years for regulated deployments
- Cross-border packaging: evidence for EU-scope customers must not leave EU storage regions unless explicit consent provided; metadata indices (hashes) may be stored in us if approved.

SDLC and deployment gating (secure-SDLC alignment)
- Any change to authorization codepaths (token broker, role managers, approval flows) must pass:
  1) Feature flag gated rollout.
  2) Automated unit + integration tests that validate audit schema invariants.
  3) Manual security review for new approval logic.
  4) Canary with observability assertions (error rate < 0.5% and missing-audit-field rate < 0.01%).
- Pre-deploy checklist (developer/owner):
  - [ ] Unit tests for audit events present
  - [ ] Audit schema backward compatibility verified
  - [ ] Config change captured in infra-as-code and tagged with change_id

Incident response integration (when delegations matter)
- Triage: If an incident involves privileged access, tag incident with delegation_id(s) and notify security_immediately channel.
- Forensic phase: SRE assembles evidence package (see manifest) and security-runbook executes chain-of-custody verification.
- Remediation: If a delegation was misused, revoke related tokens, initiate privilege recertification for impacted roles, and open a post-incident authorization review with the Authorization Owner.

Risk and exception process (decision matrix)
- Minor exceptions (low-risk): e.g., increase TTL from 1h to 4h for non-production services. Approvers: manager + service owner. Auto-close: remediation required within 14 days.
- Significant exceptions (high-risk): e.g., global read access to production logs. Approvers: security director + legal + product owner. Conditions: Must include compensating controls, monitoring hooks, and 30-day ceiling.
- Critical exceptions (emergency): break-glass flows; documented and audited with 7-day forensic review and immediate revocation after use.

Decision matrix snippet (scoring for approvals)
- Impact score (1-5): based on data sensitivity and blast radius.
- Likelihood multiplier (1-4): based on past misuse and role maturity.
- Approval threshold: exceptions scoring >12 require executive security signoff.

Automation and tooling recommendations
- Token Broker (internal): must issue JWTs with delegation_id claim and TTL, support introspection API, and emit audit events on issue/revoke.
- Evidence Orchestrator (job): scheduled jobs that run the Quarterly/Monthly cadence, export artifacts to an encrypted compliance store, and create compliance tickets automatically.
- Runbook automation: use runbooks that can be executed by SRE to generate manifest and checksums (example CLI below).

Example CLI to assemble evidence (internal tool: evidence-cli)
# gather logs and package for incident
evidence-cli assemble --incident TKT-1248 --start 2029-02-11T12:00:00Z --end 2029-02-11T18:00:00Z --region us --output s3://compliance-evidence/evidence-2029-02-11-0001

Operational SLOs and metrics to monitor
- Evidence assembly time: 90% within 48 hours (internal audit SLO).
- Missing audit field rate: <0.01% across all events.
- Delegation TTL drift (delegations granted beyond policy): 0 incidents per quarter targeted.

Post-approval obligations and remediation calendar
- Every approved exception must have a remediation ticket with owner and due date.
- Security will run automatic reminders at 7, 30, and 60 days before exception expiry.
- If remediation not completed by expiry, the system auto-revokes the exception and escalates to the security director.

Appendix A: Template approval form fields
- Requestor, Principal ID
- Role/Scope requested
- Justification, Business Impact
- TTL requested, Proposed Controls
- Approvers and Sign-off (with timestamps)
